methods.name: Peer-Median

methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring

data.narrative:
Ranovus is a Series D+ stage semiconductor company founded by Hamid Arabzadeh that has raised $236M to date, including a $36M strategic innovation fund grant in August 2025. The addressable peer universe in Chips & Semiconductors comprises 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, and Etched.

Two standard valuation triangulation methods encounter material constraints on this dataset. Peer-Median analysis is inapplicable: while 12 same-sector peers exist, none satisfy stage-matching or valuation-tier filters simultaneously—a minimum of three comparable datapoints is required for statistical reliability. Public-Comp Anchoring using the Semiconductors sector P/S median of 21.5x across the three public tickers cannot proceed without Ranovus's revenue, which private companies rarely disclose.

The absence of sufficient narrow-set comparables and missing revenue data prevents quantitative triangulation at this time. Valuation support would require either disclosure of Ranovus's revenue run rate to enable P/S anchoring, or identification of Series D+ semiconductor firms with disclosed financials to establish a defensible peer set. The $236M total capital raised establishes a floor but does not imply valuation absent clarity on deployment, burn, or unit economics. Further analysis depends on primary data collection from management.
